item.title: Georgia warehouses once planned for ICE detention centers now listed for sale after local opposition
item.description: Plans to transform warehouses in Georgia into immigration detention centres have been officially scrapped following strong backlash from local residents. Concerns raised about public safety and declining property values triggered rapid intervention from elected representatives. The General Services Administration will now proceed to auction off the previously purchased properties. Community leaders are optimistic about fostering beneficial commercial developments instead of the abandoned detention centre initiative.

item.title: Virginia boy, 9, creates autism comfort kits, named TIME's Kid of the Year
item.description: Nine-year-old Ledger Mann from Virginia has been named TIME's 2026 Kid of the Year for creating emergency comfort kits for children with autism. He started the initiative with $100 from his piggy bank after hearing about a missing child found hiding during a search operation. With support from his family and community, more than 475 kits have reached first responders across six states.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Paul Allen foundation awards third grant to historic Washington art gallery
item.description: Thanks to a generous $25,000 grant from the Allen Family Foundation, the Old Hotel Art Gallery is thriving despite financial challenges. This funding is crucial for smaller cultural organizations, allowing them to support their staff and operate effectively. With a remarkable $10 million distributed to arts organizations across Washington state, continued contributions spotlight the vital role of these institutions in fostering community engagement and heritage preservation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Ohio residents seek $3.3 million over 250 trees cut from protected forest
item.description: Ohio residents are seeking $3.3 million from the new owner of a former coal plant, alleging it cut around 250 trees from a protected greenbelt. The federal trial, which began on November 9, centres on a 1986 agreement to keep the forest substantially undisturbed. Residents say the greenbelt also helps shield their community from buried toxic coal ash near drinking-water sources.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Piddington villagers vow ‘war isn’t over’ as Rayner approves MoD Bicester asylum camp for 1,256 men
item.description: Piddington residents have vowed to continue their opposition after Angela Rayner approved plans to accommodate 1,256 male asylum seekers at the former military site, MoD Bicester. Despite the planning approval, villagers are considering legal action, insisting their fight is far from over. The Home Office says a final decision on the site's use is still pending.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Josh Hokit vows no regret over vulgar Michelle Obama remarks ahead of UFC title fight
item.description: UFC heavyweight Josh Hokit has refused to apologise for his controversial remarks about former US first lady Michelle Obama, insisting he has no regrets despite widespread backlash. The undefeated fighter defended making the comments at the White House, claiming the controversy boosted his profile. Hokit now turns his attention to Ciryl Gane and his first UFC heavyweight title opportunity at UFC 334.

item.title: Kansas sues to halt public funding for $160M lagoon resort still without buildings
item.description: In a significant move, Kansas state officials have filed a lawsuit aimed at halting any further public bond financing for the stalled Derby Shores project, a $160 million lagoon resort. Despite receiving approval four years ago, construction has yet to commence. The suit seeks to prevent new bond payments and mandates a detailed financial report on bonds already issued, raising concerns over taxpayer exposure from the ongoing delays.

item.title: A Dallas woman turns a $5.99 Goodwill find into $17,500
item.description: During a routine shopping trip at Goodwill in Dallas, a lucky resident stumbled upon a rare woodcut by Gustave Baumann for just $5.99. After some investigative research, she uncovered that the piece, titled Bright Angel Trail, was from a limited edition and signed by the artist himself. Ultimately, the artwork fetched an astounding $17,500 at auction, despite minor condition issues, transforming her ordinary day into a remarkable moment of discovery.

item.title: Former Fox host Maria Bartiromo sells $6.5M Manhattan townhouse for $7M
item.description: In a notable real estate transaction, Maria Bartiromo and her spouse, Jonathan Steinberg, finalized the sale of their Manhattan townhouse for a hefty $7 million. This sale occurred confidentially shortly after Bartiromo's departure from Fox News Media, following over 12 years with the network. Having purchased the five-storey residence nearly 19 years ago for $6.5 million, they faced a monetary loss when adjusted for inflation.

item.title: Inheritance Dispute Ruling: judge voids Douglass will; elder son may get $1bn estate
item.description: In a recent legal development, Lanzce Douglass and Stacey Douglass Boies have been found by the court to have financially taken advantage of their father, Harlan Douglass. The judge has reinstated Harlan's earlier will, raising Harley Douglass's chances of inheriting a substantial fortune. This inheritance dispute sheds light on the complexity of wealth distribution, revealing cognitive struggles that affected Harlan's financial decisions.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 72-year-old's restaurant was struggling; then a stranger's video changed everything
item.description: A viral Instagram video by content creator Robert Schrott brought unexpected support to Greek's Grill, a struggling family restaurant in Chandler, Arizona. Owner Fred Najour, 72, saw customers line up within days, while a fundraiser started by Schrott raised more than $19,000.
